title: Project registry
description: The projects the studio operates, and the boundary around each one. JARVIS is the studio layer; a project is a product underneath it. This file is what makes that separation checkable rather than merely intended: each project declares the paths it owns, and WorkforceCrossCheckTests refuses overlapping ownership and refuses any project claiming a path inside the studio layer. The rule it enforces in both directions is the founder's: studio tooling never ships inside a product, and no product's internals leak into the studio layer. A second project is added by appending an entry here -- not by restructuring anything above it.

studioPaths.description: Paths belonging to the studio layer itself -- the kernel, the constitution, the gate machinery and the cockpit. No project may claim any of these, and the studio layer must not reach into a project's own source beyond the verification paths a gate needs.

repo.description: The GitHub repository the project lives in, as owner/name. Absent means the project shares this repository with the studio layer, which is how things stood before JARVIS was separated. Present and different from the studio's own repository means the project is external: its files must NOT exist here, and NoProjectOwnedPathExistsInTheStudioRepository enforces exactly that. This field is the integration boundary -- JARVIS refers to a project rather than containing it.

ref.description: The branch or tag JARVIS treats as this project's current state. Only meaningful alongside repo. It is deliberately a name rather than a commit: a pinned SHA would make the studio's view of a project go stale silently, and the whole point of naming a ref is that the project moves under it.

owns.description: The paths this project owns. Nothing outside them is the project's, and nothing inside them belongs to the studio layer.

verifiedByGates.description: Which gates rule on this project. A project with no gate has no definition of done.

divisions.description: Divisions currently doing work on this project. Absent means the whole roster may serve it.

allOf.description: A ref names a point inside a repository. Without repo there is nothing for it to name, and a lone ref would read as though the studio tracked a branch it has no way to reach.
